title: Trust-Aware UAV Resource Allocation for Disaster-Responsive IoMT Communication Networks via Adaptive Reinforcement-Assisted Learning
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Trust-Aware UAV Resource Allocation for Disaster-Responsive IoMT Communication Networks via Adaptive Reinforcement-Assisted Learning

keywords: AI and Machine Learning in IoMT

detail.abstract: Disaster affected regions often experience severe disruption of terrestrial communication and medical infrastructure, which significantly reduces the reliability of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) healthcare services. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can provide rapid aerial connectivity and mobile edge support in such environments. However, limited onboard energy, UAV activation overhead, service latency requirements, and heterogeneous trust levels introduce a challenging resource allocation problem. This work presents a trust aware optimization framework that jointly minimizes normalized operational, activation, and latency costs while maximizing service reliability under energy, capacity, and trust eligibility constraints. The problem is formulated as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model that serves as an optimal benchmark. To enable scalable optimization, the model is complemented by the Adaptive Reinforcement Assisted Probabilistic Learning Algorithm (ARPLA), which combines probabilistic exploration with reinforcement guided adaptation. Simulation based evaluations across varying device densities, trust thresholds, UAV fleet sizes, and service diversity demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results indicate that ARPLA achieves near optimal performance with polynomial time complexity and maintains a solution quality within 3-9% of the optimal benchmark. Compared with conventional approaches, the proposed method reduces normalized total cost by up to 90% relative to the Greedy strategy and by more than 35% compared with reinforcement based methods, while the average performance ratio between ARPLA and the optimal solution reaches 0.993 in joint trust and load sensitivity analysis.

title: The Norwegian Monarchy under Strain: Symbolic Boundary Collapse and Institutional Legitimacy in the Platform Age
affiliations: University of South-Eastern Norway USN School of Business

detail.title: The Norwegian Monarchy under Strain: Symbolic Boundary Collapse and Institutional Legitimacy in the Platform Age
detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines how symbolic institutions become vulnerable to legitimacy strain under platformized media conditions, using the Norwegian monarchy as an illustrative case. Design/methodology/approach: The paper is conceptual. It develops a framework of symbolic boundary collapse by integrating branding theory, symbolic capital, parasociality, institutional legitimacy, and crisis communication. The framework is applied illustratively to the Norwegian monarchy and briefly compared with selected European monarchy cases. Findings: The analysis shows that legitimacy strain is shaped by the interaction of four dimensions: severity of misconduct, symbolic proximity, institutional centrality, and baseline symbolic capital. Platformized media environments amplify adjacency, emotional salience, and moral clarity, weakening formal distinctions between institutions and symbolically proximate actors. The Norwegian case illustrates how cumulative boundary stress can emerge even in a high-trust context when high-severity peripheral scandal and lower-severity but high-centrality adjacency converge. Practical implications: The framework suggests that symbolic institutions should treat adjacency as a governance problem and calibrate distancing, empathy, and procedural framing according to actor centrality and legitimacy reserves. Originality/value: The paper contributes a theory of symbolic boundary collapse that shifts attention from responsibility to association as a mechanism of legitimacy erosion. It extends organizational analysis by showing how platformized visibility reshapes reputational risk for institutions whose authority depends on symbolic legitimacy rather than instrumental performance.

title: Moral Philosophy and Archetypes in the Symbolic Cohesion of the Sleeping Beauty's Airplane Tale
affiliations: and

detail.title: Moral Philosophy and Archetypes in the Symbolic Cohesion of the Sleeping Beauty's Airplane Tale
detail.abstract: This study examines the moralizing value of the short story The Airplane of the Sleeping Beauty by Gabriel García Márquez through an interdisciplinary approach that integrates literature, moral philosophy, and sociology. The narrator’s behavior toward the sleeping woman is interpreted as a symbolic scenario in which tensions between desire, social norms, and ethical responsibility emerge. The analysis engages with Aristotelian virtue ethics, John Stuart Mill’s utilitarianism, Immanuel Kant’s deontological ethics, and Émile Durkheim’s sociology of moral norms, as well as Hobbesian and Machiavellian reflections on fear as a foundation of social order. The narrative demonstrates how moral consciousness, self-restraint, and respect for human dignity operate as cultural mechanisms that sustain social cohesion.

title: Beyond Legacy: The Case for Enduring Impact Organizations
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: Beyond Legacy: The Case for Enduring Impact Organizations
detail.abstract: The term enduring impact appears in leadership commentary, strategic planning documents, consulting frameworks and impact measurement conversations. In most cases, it is used to describe outcomes that last, such as programs whose benefits continue beyond their funding period or initiatives that generate sustained change in communities. This emphasis on duration is important since impact measured only in short-term outputs is incomplete. Social and environmental challenges unfold over long time horizons and durable change requires more than temporary activity. Prevailing uses of enduring impact share a common limitation: they focus on the persistence of results rather than the durability of the organization producing those results. This article makes the argument for ensuring that the organization itself is intentionally designed to last and deliver impact across generations.

title: Indecision and Decision Paralysis in the Digital Age

detail.title: Indecision and Decision Paralysis in the Digital Age
detail.abstract: Why does having more options so often leave people feeling worse, not better? That question sits at the centre of this paper. Two decades of research on the Paradox of Choice-the empirically documented reversal in which choice abundance undermines rather than enhances well-being-have produced a robust directional finding without fully explaining who suffers most, or why digital environments appear to intensify the effect. This paper argues that Intolerance of Uncertainty (IU) is the dispositional key that links choice overload to chronic indecision, and that contemporary digital platforms are structured in ways that activate IU rather than relieve it. Through a qualitative meta-synthesis of peer-reviewed literature from 2000 to 2024-drawing exclusively on verified, DOI-resolvable sources-the paper reconstructs the cognitive and emotional pathway from digital abundance to decision paralysis, identifies meaningful gaps in the existing literature, and proposes both research priorities and practical directions for ethical platform design.

title: An Empirical Investigation of Long-run IPO Underperformance on the National Stock Exchange of India
affiliations: KeplerX Aviation

detail.title: An Empirical Investigation of Long-run IPO Underperformance on the National Stock Exchange of India
detail.abstract:
• This paper presents an empirical investigation of the long-run performance of Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) of India between January 2020 and December 2023, relative to the NIFTY 50 benchmark index. A sample of 147 mainboard IPOs is analysed across three dimensions: (1) 12-month excess returns relative to the NIFTY 50; (2) sectoral variation in post-listing performance; and (3) the moderating role of IPO size, oversubscription levels, and Offer for Sale (OFS) proportion on long-run returns. 
• The study finds that 68.7% of sampled IPOs generated negative excess returns (underperformed the NIFTY 50) in the twelve months following listing, with a mean excess return of-6.3 percentage points. Underperformance is most pronounced in the consumer internet and fintech sectors, in IPOs with NII oversubscription exceeding 30x, and in issues where OFS constitutes more than 60% of total issue size. The findings are consistent with the global 'new issues puzzle' documented by Ritter (1991) and Loughran and Ritter (1995), and extend this literature to India's post-COVID capital market context.
• The paper argues that structural features of India's primary market-including aggressive OFS-driven pricing, leverage-fuelled speculative demand, and SEBI's pre-2022 allotment mechanism-systematically contribute to post-listing underperformance. SEBI's April 2022 regulatory reforms partially addressed these structural issues, as evidenced by a measurable reduction in NII oversubscription and short-term flipping behaviour post-reform.

title: Scalable Stochastic Model for Sea Cargo Revenue Management with Empty Container Transportation
affiliations: , United Institute of Informatics Problems, United Institute of Informatics Problems, Queen's University,  and Queen's University - Smith School of Business

detail.title: Scalable Stochastic Model for Sea Cargo Revenue Management with Empty Container Transportation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest to declare.

detail.abstract: This study addresses freight revenue management in the container shipping industry, a domain characterized by unique modeling challenges arising from its complex operational structure and multiple sources of uncertainty. Building on recent advances in subgradient optimization, we develop a scalable stochastic model that captures both long-term and short-term decision elements, including dynamic pricing, overbooking, container allocation, and empty container repositioning. Our approach extends the Lagrangian relaxation framework previously applied to air cargo to sea freight, incorporating interspersed period types, hub and weight constraints, and scalability via convex non-smooth optimization. In addition, we design two large-scale algorithms that optimize pricing and container management in both spot and allotment market stages. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the practical potential of our approach: algorithms recommend repositioning empty containers with volumes nearly double those traded in the spot market, revealing substantial untapped revenue opportunities through integrated optimization.

title: Canada Needs Informed Economic Diversification to Navigate in a Turbulent World
affiliations: Sasin School of Management, Chulalongkorn University and

detail.title: Canada Needs Informed Economic Diversification to Navigate in a Turbulent World
detail.abstract: Canada is facing a pivotal moment. In these turbulent times, traditional economic relations are in transition. Canada’s response requires an effective and well thought out external economic strategy, including diversification of economic relations.  But unless such diversification rests on careful analysis, it risks at best being ineffective, at worst counterproductive. Canada’s two diversification priorities, China and Europe, as well as emerging economic corridors reshaping global trade, further illustrate why such analysis is indispensable for effective economic diversification.

title:
Learning Stabilizing Policies for Multimodal Transportation Networks: 
A Capacity Geometry and Foster-Lyapunov Framework

detail.title:
Learning Stabilizing Policies for Multimodal Transportation Networks: 
A Capacity Geometry and Foster-Lyapunov Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Modern multimodal transportation networks operate in highly stochastic environments where localized capacity disruptions can propagate into cascading hyper-congestion. Classical equilibrium and dynamic traffic assignment models struggle to manage these nonlinear dynamics without relying on computationally intensive centralized optimization. 

This paper develops a mathematical framework for the endogenous stabilization of multimodal transportation networks under decentralized control. We first formalize the feasible operating domain of the network as a stochastic capacity region whose boundary evolves under bounded infrastructure degradation. This representation provides a geometric characterization of feasible traffic states and establishes structural bounds on network throughput under uncertainty. 

Building on this formulation, we derive a topologically weighted Foster-Lyapunov drift inequality for multimodal traffic dynamics governed by actual-discharge queueing models. The analysis proves that decentralized routing policies satisfying a negative expected overload drift condition guarantee stability of the network state relative to the interior of the capacity region.

 We further show that any parameterized decentralized policy class that sufficiently approximates the stabilizing controller, including cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) inherits the same Foster-Lyapunov stability property. 

Controlled numerical experiments on a benchmark multimodal topology empirically validate the theoretical bounds. The results demonstrate that learned decentralized policies preserve the network's macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) and autonomously restore the system to the safe capacity interior following severe stochastic capacity shocks.

title: Beyond Partisanship: Governance and the Structural Mechanics of the Sustainable Development Framework (TBL) Deus Servet Trochleam
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Partisanship: Governance and the Structural Mechanics of the Sustainable Development Framework (TBL) Deus Servet Trochleam
detail.abstract: This paper examines the theory of the Sustainable Development Framework, also known as the Triple Bottom Line (TBL), and finds that it is widely invoked as a sustainability paradigm integrating environmental integrity, social legitimacy, and economic vitality. Yet persistent instability across these pillars suggests that conceptual recognition alone does not ensure balance. The paper argues that the effectiveness of the TBL depends not upon rhetorical commitment but upon the quality of governance mechanisms that calibrate competing interests and internalise cross-domain externalities. Drawing on institutional analysis and practitioner experience across public administration, resource economies, and fiscal policy, the paper examines how governance structures influence system stability. It demonstrates that imbalance arises when decision-making is distorted by partisan competition within government structures, regulatory capture, or shortterm political incentives. Conversely, where government operates with transparency, accountability, and impartial stewardship, fiscal and regulatory instruments can maintain equilibrium between environmental sustainability, social cohesion, and economic productivity. It reframes the TBL as a structural stability framework rather than a normative aspiration. It concludes that sustainable development requires governance capable of acting without fear or favour, maintaining institutional continuity, and resisting capture by any single domain. In this sense, impartial governance is not a moral preference but a functional necessity for system resilience.

title: When Disaster Strikes Y’all Street: A Study on Cross-Sector Collaboration in Protecting U.S. Financial Critical Infrastructure
affiliations: John Jay College - CUNY Graduate Center and City University of New York (CUNY) - John Jay College

detail.title: When Disaster Strikes Y’all Street: A Study on Cross-Sector Collaboration in Protecting U.S. Financial Critical Infrastructure

PI: Rachael Zerr IRB ID: 2025-0443-JohnJay Title: When Disaster Strikes Y’all Street: A Study on Cross-Sector Collaboration in Protecting U.S. Financial Critical Infrastructure Funding: No funding Funding ID: No funding Exempt category(ies): 45CFR46.104(2)

detail.abstract: This exploratory research examines public-private collaboration between corporate security leaders and local emergency responders in the North Texas financial corridor known as “Y’all Street.” Using perception-based survey data from senior representatives in the private and public sectors, the paper evaluates partnership strength, preparedness activities, information sharing, and operational coordination. Findings indicate that collaborative practices such as facility tours, joint exercises, and emergency planning are present, but that partnership maturity remains uneven and is not yet fully standardized across the corridor. The research concludes that more formalized and institutionalized coordination will be necessary to strengthen resilience as the region’s financial significance and threat exposure continue to expand.

title: Chapter 4 : MONEY ATTITUDE
affiliations: University of Skovde - School of Business

detail.title: Chapter 4 : MONEY ATTITUDE
detail.abstract: This chapter examines the idea of money attitude and describes it as a multidimensional psychological concept that influences how individuals interpret, value, and handle money in everyday life. It highlights that money is not only an economic resource but also a symbolic object associated with security, power, status, freedom, achievement, and emotional meaning. The chapter outlines the historical development of money attitude research, reviews its key dimensions, and discusses the main instruments used to measure it, including the Money Attitude Scale (MAS), the Money Beliefs and Behaviors Scale (MBBS), and the Money Ethic Scale (MES). It also synthesized the major factors that shape money attitudes, such as family financial socialization, childhood financial experiences, personality traits, demographic characteristics, and cultural context. Finally, the chapter discusses how money attitudes influence financial behavior and well-being, including saving, spending, compulsive buying, gambling, investment decisions, financial literacy, workplace outcomes, and financial distress in consumer finance contexts.

title: Employee Equity and Workforce Outcomes in Startups: Evidence from Binding Wage Constraints
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - Management Department and IESE Business School

detail.title: Employee Equity and Workforce Outcomes in Startups: Evidence from Binding Wage Constraints
detail.abstract: How do binding wage constraints reshape ownership allocation in startups, and what are the consequences for employee retention and internal mobility? Young firms trade off ownership dilution against scarce internal liquidity when compensating workers, making employee equity an endogenous component of their financing and ownership structure. Yet little is known about how constraints on cash compensation affect employee equity allocation or how employee ownership influences workforce outcomes. Using population-wide administrative data from Finland covering all limited liability startups that reach at least 10 employees between 2006 and 2022, we track annual equity stakes for founders, employees, managers, and outside investors. To identify causal effects, we exploit staggered introductions and removals of industry-level collective bargaining agreement (CBA) extensions that raise mandated wage floors for previously uncovered firms. These regulatory changes tighten or relax cash compensation constraints, providing plausibly exogenous variation in wages and employee equity. We find that CBA extensions reduce individual employee equity stakes by 10-11%, consistent with startups conserving ownership under tighter wage constraints. Instrumental variables estimates indicate that a 10% increase in employee equity reduces one-year exit by 2.5-3% and increases internal advancement by 10-12%. Effects are weaker in high-technology industries. Overall, binding wage constraints systematically reshape the allocation of employee ownership, and employee equity causally shapes workforce retention and advancement in young firms.

title: Delegated Financial Cognition (DFC) in Digital Financial Platforms: A Process Theory of Agency, Trust and Bias behavior in Agentic Fintech

detail.title: Delegated Financial Cognition (DFC) in Digital Financial Platforms: A Process Theory of Agency, Trust and Bias behavior in Agentic Fintech
detail.abstract: The increasing integration of agentic artificial intelligence into digital financial platforms and electronic markets, such as robo-advisors, AI-driven credit systems, and conversational financial agents, is transforming how financial decisions are made and executed. These systems extend beyond traditional decision support by exhibiting goal-directed behavior, adaptive learning, and autonomous execution, functioning as quasi-independent decision agents within digital financial ecosystems. As a result, users increasingly delegate evaluative financial reasoning to algorithmic systems, shifting the locus of cognition from human decision-makers to platform-embedded intelligence.  This paper develops a process theory of Delegated Financial Cognition (DFC) to explain how perceived algorithmic agency induces cognitive delegation, reduces user monitoring, and shapes trust calibration in agentic fintech market environments. The framework further theorizes how miscalibrated trust interacts with behavioral biases, leading to amplification or attenuation effects in financial decision outcomes. The study formalizes possible research propositions and identify boundary conditions across technological (e.g., transparency, explainability), human (e.g., financial literacy, algorithm familiarity), and environmental (e.g., market volatility, decision complexity) dimensions. By integrating behavioral finance, trust in automation, and information systems research, the study aims to contribute an explanation of how human-AI decision processes occur on agentic fintech platforms. The findings look to advance understanding of digital financial services by conceptualizing cognitive delegation as a core mechanism underlying emerging forms of embedded and contextual financial decision-making.

title: Plugging into Confidence: How Platform Interoperability Reshapes Electric Vehicle Charging Behavior and Charging Network Efficiency
affiliations: Nanjing University, University of Georgia - C. Herman and Mary Virginia Terry College of Business, Terry College of Business, the University of Georgia, University of Georgia - Department of Management Information Systems and Nanjing University

detail.title: Plugging into Confidence: How Platform Interoperability Reshapes Electric Vehicle Charging Behavior and Charging Network Efficiency
detail.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging platforms face a persistent utilization paradox: charging capacity remains idle for much of the day but experiences substantial peak-time congestion. Infrastructure expansion alone is insufficient to resolve this imbalance, as demand concentration stems not only from capacity constraints but also from users' limited view of available charging options and the resultant precautionary charging behavior. We examine platform interoperability that allows users to discover and access charging stations across rival platforms. Such initiative, however, presents critical tension as it intensifies demandside competition without generating conventional supply-side benefits (e.g., cost reduction or product innovation) considered in the extant literature. Therefore, its value for a focal platform remains theoretically unclear. Our research presents a novel insight by empirically showing how EV platform interoperability, by engendering structural transparency within the charging network, benefits a focal platform through mitigating demand-side behavioral signatures consistent with range anxiety. Leveraging a quasi-experimental setting of leading Chinese EV charging platforms, we find that interoperability makes EV users initiate charging at lower battery levels, recover less range per session, and shift a significant share of charging from peak to off-peak periods. These behavioral adjustments aggregate into station-level utilization efficiency such as lower demand fluctuation and a load shift from peak to off-peak hours. More importantly, these improvements lead to better financial performance, including reduced peak-time electricity costs and increased overall revenue-to-cost ratios. Collectively, our findings advance the understanding of platform interoperability by showing how it alleviates demand-side behaviorallydriven inefficiencies to enhance both platform performance and shared infrastructure efficiency.

title: Understanding Access to Fish Feed Among Smallholder Farmers: A Partial Proportional Odds Logit Approach Applied to Kenya Aquaculture Farmers
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology, Maseno University - Maseno University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Understanding Access to Fish Feed Among Smallholder Farmers: A Partial Proportional Odds Logit Approach Applied to Kenya Aquaculture Farmers
detail.abstract: AbstractFish feed remains the most critical input in aquaculture, constituting up to 80% of production costs and influencing economic and ecological performance, yet systematic evidence on the extent of feed access at the farm level remains poorly documented in sub-Saharan Africa. This study introduces a Farm Feed Insecurity Access Scale, conceptually inspired by the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale, to measure the extent of fish feed constraints among small-scale aquaculture households in Kenya. The FFIAS captures four domains - anxiety, compromised quality, insufficient quantity, and severe deprivation - through farmer self-reports over a production cycle. Data were collected from 847 aquaculture households through face-to-face surveys administered using KoBo Collect. Results revealed that while many smallholder farmers were feed secure, nearly half experienced mild to moderate insecurity, and a small but important minority reported severe outcomes such as ration cuts, and reliance on inferior substitutes. To explore the determinants of feed access insecurity, a Partial Proportional Odds Logit model was estimated, relaxing the proportional odds assumption where necessary. Results show that larger household size, extreme poverty, and greater distance to feed markets significantly increased the probability of moderate and severe insecurity, while higher education, income diversification, and use of digital tools enhanced feed security. Institutional factors – including formal aquaculture training, cooperative membership, extension access, and credit –reduced the likelihood of severe insecurity. Knowledge of locally available feed ingredients, information usefulness, and understanding of feed nutrition also played critical roles, whereas development support showed mixed effects. These findings underscore the multidimensional nature of feed insecurity and highlight the importance of strengthening institutional support, resource access, and aquaculture knowledge systems to enhance farm resilience and sustainability in small-scale aquaculture in Kenya and similar regions.

title: BEPS and Nepalese Taxation
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: BEPS and Nepalese Taxation
detail.abstract: Background Gaps and mismatches in the current international tax rules can make profits "disappear" for tax purposes, or allow the shifting of profits to no or low-tax locations where the business has little or no economic activity 1. These activities are referred to as base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS). Questions have also been raised on the tax planning practices of MNCs like Google, Starbucks etc, in Europe. The schemes of planning may carry different names, however, the aim and end of these schemes is to pay no or low tax. Though academics and tax authorities repeatedly grill the MNCs regarding these practices, they, by large walk scot free.

title: Granular Games with P-Liquid Atomic Masses
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School

detail.title: Granular Games with P-Liquid Atomic Masses
detail.abstract: Fix 0 < p < 1. This project is an adventure in games with countably many heterogeneous players with ℓ^p-summable weights and whose mixed strategies satisfy a uniform ℓ^p bound. The class is motivated by the free p-liquid modules of Clausen and Scholze. Our main discovery is a bounded aggregation theorem: if player weights are ℓ^p-summable and each player's mixed strategy satisfies a common ℓ^p bound, the aggregate distribution inherits that bound with a clean constant. We also record that for a fixed aggregate, mixing never helps, and pure strategies will suffice. Equilibrium existence in the finite case follows from Kakutani.

title: Child and Caregiver Food Insecurity Reports: Differential Associations with Child Skills
affiliations: Princeton University, University of Barcelona and University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: Child and Caregiver Food Insecurity Reports: Differential Associations with Child Skills
detail.abstract: Two out of three children in low-income countries are affected by food insecurity. Household food insecurity is typically measured using caregiver reports, but children reports may shed light on experiences or domains of food insecurity overlooked by caregivers. Using a novel validated measure of child-reported food insecurity, we examine how both child- and caregiver-reported food insecurity predict children's academic, cognitive, and socioemotional skills in a large sample of children (N = 3,771, ages 5–17) and their caregivers in five northern Ghana regions. Caregivers were nearly twice as likely as children to report food insecurity, with larger discrepancies across items reflecting moderate food insecurity manifestations. In value-added models that aim to control for unobserved heterogeneity driving skills, caregiver-reported food insecurity predicted lower literacy and numeracy, especially for boys and older adolescents, whereas child-reported food insecurity was not predictive of any outcome. Potential mechanisms (child health, parental educational investments, children's aspirations, and caregiver psychological well-being) partially accounted for the observed associations. Findings suggest that caregiver reports better capture the constraints induced by food insecurity on children's learning in this context, which is important information for the targeting of interventions to support child development via tackling food insecurity.

title:
How Generative AI can Harm Higher Education, 
with Special Emphasis on Legal Education
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
How Generative AI can Harm Higher Education, 
with Special Emphasis on Legal Education
detail.abstract:
Generative AI has the potential to do catastrophic harm to higher education.   This is because learning is a biological process that requires years and years of effortful labor.  Anything that disrupts this labor will severely damage an individual’s ability to function in the world.  Gen AI is such a disruption because it substitutes efficiency for learning.  Nothing can compensate for the losses incurred when Gen AI is used instead of the human brain.

The problem with Gen AI performing learning tasks rather than the student is that there is no learning.  This lack of learning applies to both basic and advanced learning.  Over reliance on Gen AI produces less factual knowledge and process knowledge than traditional learning in long-term memory—potentially much less knowledge. In addition, it could significantly harm advanced learning.  To begin, advanced learning requires a foundation in the brain.  Experts have much, much greater factual and procedural knowledge than novices.  If such basic knowledge does not exist in the brain (long-term memory), one cannot become an expert.  There is no way that an individual can make up for a lack of basic knowledge in long-term memory—not by using Wikipedia or Gen AI.  Basic knowledge must be internal for advanced thinking.  Similarly, students cannot imprint advanced thinking techniques on their brains if Gen AI does the work for them.

title: The Problem of Waste-Part 1: The Resource Conservation and Recovery Act

detail.title: The Problem of Waste-Part 1: The Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
detail.abstract:
Scared of RCRA?  We've got you covered!  This chapter walks readers through the history of RCRA, its major components, and offers suggestions for how to teach this statute effectively. 

Waste is ubiquitous. We all generate it, and we all throw it away. Yet, for many students (and their teachers), RCRA (and CERCLA) are the dryest, least comprehensible environmental statutes. The way we typically cover these statutes in an environmental law class does not help—most environmental law classes devote little time to underlying consumption/waste issues, limiting coverage to the handful of legal issues that sparked litigation during the early years of RCRA and CERCLA. Like so much of environmental law, the tendency is to immerse students in complex legal analysis, arcane regulatory schemes, and landmark cases from the distant past. This litigation framing results in highly abstract classroom discussions, making it difficult for students to appreciate the profound justice challenges embedded in these laws and regulations. 

This chapter offers something different because RCRA provides the rare opportunity to start class discussions with something personal and immediately recognizable: the daily generation and disposal of waste. Starting here can help students bridge the gap between legal theory and its practical implementation. Moreover, because waste is something tangible that is managed at the local level, RCRA offers the opportunity to delve more deeply into the model of cooperative federalism at the heart of so much environmental law. Multi-level governance creates both challenges and opportunities that are not apparent from reading appellate cases but are very visible in tracing the fate and transport of specific wastes.

title: Fixed-k Inference for Spot R-squared in High-frequency Factor Models
affiliations: Jinan University - College of Economics

detail.title: Fixed-k Inference for Spot R-squared in High-frequency Factor Models
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel fixed-k econometric framework for nonparametric inference on the instantaneous coefficient of determination, the spot R-squared, in continuous-time factor models. Unlike conventional large-k asymptotics, which suffer from smoothing bias and rely on unstable nuisance parameters, we formulate local regression as a finite-sample Gaussian limit experiment. We show that the spot R-squared estimator converges to a random variable with a hierarchical noncentral F distribution. This pivotal limit theory facilitates exact local inference that is completely free of nuisance parameters and asymptotically Uniformly Most Powerful Invariant (UMPI). Furthermore, we establish uniform confidence bands for the entire spot R-squared trajectory by coupling the non-Donsker functional limit with extreme value theory. Illustrating the practical utility of our methodology, we formalize a high-frequency Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) to test for structural breaks around FOMC announcements and document abrupt, market-wide algorithmic herding triggered by macroeconomic shocks.

title: Exploring the Role of Local Agriculture-based Civil Society Organizations in Addressing Child Trafficking in Ghana's Cocoa Industry: A Qualitative Case Study
affiliations: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana and Independent Researcher

detail.title: Exploring the Role of Local Agriculture-based Civil Society Organizations in Addressing Child Trafficking in Ghana's Cocoa Industry: A Qualitative Case Study
detail.abstract: This qualitative case study explores the contributions and constraints of local agriculture-based Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) in addressing child trafficking within Ghana's cocoa industry in the Ashanti Region. Through in-depth interviews with 20 participants—10 cocoa farmers, 8 government officials, and 2 CSO actors—the study examines CSO interventions, operational challenges, and potential strategies for enhanced effectiveness. Findings reveal that local CSOs engage in critical activities, including victim rescue, community sensitization, and policy advocacy. However, their efforts are significantly constrained by funding instability, institutional marginalization, weak state collaboration, and geographic isolation. The study employs Migration Theory and Vulnerability Theory to explain how structural vulnerabilities and institutional fragilities perpetuate child trafficking despite CSO interventions. The research identifies five key strategies for strengthening CSO effectiveness: establishing sustainable funding mechanisms, enhancing institutional collaboration, investing in culturally sensitive behavior change programs, developing legal protections for CSO actors, and building capacity through training and digital resources. Findings contribute to understanding how child protection services can be strengthened in agricultural supply chains and inform broader civil society engagement strategies in vulnerable communities.

title: From Wearables to Telemedicine: Industry 4.0' S Influence on Health Care Delivery
affiliations: and

detail.title: From Wearables to Telemedicine: Industry 4.0' S Influence on Health Care Delivery
detail.abstract: Technology has played a pivotal role in all the fields .Technology has the potential to improve the quality, safety and efficiency in every sector. Healthcare changes dramatically because of technological developments, from anesthetics and antibiotics to magnetic resonance imaging scanners and radiotherapy Advancements in healthcare capabilities are due to significant progress in available technologies. Integrating these technologies into each division of healthcare can benefit patients and medical staff. Proper knowledge and implementation of these new tools can push a health organization to a new level of success. This paper focuses on the impact of technological integration in health care .Technologies had a significant impact on healthcare and the delivery of health services. From Telemedicine to electronic health records ,a variety of healthcare services have been shown to improve operational and administrative efficiencies, clinical outcomes, documentation and information flow in a global settings, home care units, rural health centers and large urban hospitals. Technological innovation in future is going to keep transforming healthcare, while these technologies (new drugs and treatments, new devices, new social media support for healthcare, etc) will drive innovation, human factors will remain one of the stable limitations. No predictions can satisfy everybody; instead, this article explores fragments of the future to see how to think more clearly about how to get where we want to go.

title: Retail Price Parity as a Channel-Coordination Mechanism in Dual Distribution
affiliations: Compass Lexecon, Yale University, Compass Lexecon and Econic Partners

detail.title: Retail Price Parity as a Channel-Coordination Mechanism in Dual Distribution
detail.abstract: When a manufacturer distributes its products through both a direct sales channel and an independent retailer, a fundamental tension arises between the efficiencies of direct distribution and the need to incentivize the retailer. To induce the retailer to undertake noncontractible actions that enhance demand, such as pre-and post-sale assistance, the manufacturer must grant it a high gross margin. This, however, creates incentives for the manufacturer to undercut the retailer ex post through its direct channel. We show that a retail price parity (RPP) policy, which requires identical retail prices across the direct and independent channels, can increase the manufacturer's and the retailer's joint profits. By allowing the manufacturer to commit not to undercut the retailer, RPP strengthens the retailer's incentives to undertake valuable noncontractible actions and enables supply contracts that increase joint profits. Because higher effort improves service quality, RPP may also increase consumer welfare even when it leads to higher monetary retail prices. These findings offer guidance for managers designing dual distribution strategies and inform policy discussions on the competitive effects of price-parity clauses.

title: Multivariate GARCH and Portfolio Variance Prediction: A Forecast Reconciliation Perspective
affiliations: University of Padua - Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Padova and University of Padova

detail.title: Multivariate GARCH and Portfolio Variance Prediction: A Forecast Reconciliation Perspective

declarations.funderStatement: The authors acknowledge financial support from project PRIN2022 PRICE: A New Paradigm for High-Frequency Finance, 2022C799SX. This study was funded by the European Union-NextGeneration EU, Mission 4, Component 2, in the framework of the GRINS-Growing Resilient, INclusive and Sustainable project [grant numbers GRINS PE00000018-CUP C93C22005270001].

detail.abstract: We assess the advantage of combining univariate and multivariate portfolio risk forecasts with the aid of forecast reconciliation techniques. In our analyzes, we assume knowledge of portfolio weights, a standard for portfolio risk management applications. With an extensive simulation experiment, we show that, if the true covariance is known, forecast reconciliation improves over a standard multivariate approach, in particular when the adopted multivariate model is misspecified. However, if noisy proxies are used, correctly specified models and the misspecified ones (for instance, neglecting spillovers) turn out to be, in several cases, indistinguishable, with forecast reconciliation still providing improvements, even though smaller. The noise in the covariance proxy plays a crucial role in determining the improvement of both the forecast reconciliation and the correct model specification. An empirical analysis shows how forecast reconciliation can be adopted with real data to improve traditional GARCH-based portfolio variance forecasts.

title: Fiscal And Monetary Policy During the Pandemic in Canada: A Quantitative Analysis
affiliations: and University of Windsor

detail.title: Fiscal And Monetary Policy During the Pandemic in Canada: A Quantitative Analysis
detail.abstract: We build a two-agent New Keynesian (TANK) model, augmented with the central bank balance sheet and government budget constraint, to quantify macroeconomic effects of the fiscal and monetary stimulus measures in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic. The model is calibrated to the Canadian economy, and shock processes are estimated. The model closely replicates the observed dynamics of the economy over the pandemic period. Counterfactual experiments reveal that transfer payments played a key role in cushioning the initial contraction by supporting the consumption of hand-to-mouth (HtM) households, while forward guidance and quantitative easing strengthen these effects through the investment channel and by forestalling a severe deflationary episode. At the same time, the prolonged maintenance of low policy interest rate, in conjunction with large-scale fiscal transfers, contributed substantially to the post-pandemic surge in inflation. We show that an earlier normalization of monetary policy would have significantly reduced post-pandemic inflation at only modest cost to output, suggesting that a more gradual tightening path could have reduced the need for the aggressive interest rate increases that followed.

title: Interest Expenses and Commercial Expediency Test
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Interest Expenses and Commercial Expediency Test
detail.abstract: Interest expenses and Commercial Expediency Test Prof. HLA Hart famously stated that 'whichever device, precedent or legislation, is chosen for the communication of standards of behavior, these, however smoothly they work over the great mass of ordinary cases, will, at some point where their application is in question, prove indeterminate; they will have what has been termed an open texture.' 1 Hart borrowed the concept of open texture from Friedrich Waismann who went even further to state that even the most precise and carefully delimited empirical terms might nevertheless produce uncertainty in the face of unforeseen and virtually unimaginable instances. Because language cannot anticipate all possible occurrences in all possible worlds, he argued, there persists the ineliminable potential that a definition of an empirical concept bounded in all now-foreseeable dimensions can break down in the face of unforeseen and unforeseeable events because of language. 2 Even the words that seemingly, at first sight, have no ambiguities or vagueness might offer differing interpretations. This article focuses on one such instance-the phrase, 'incurred in the production of income from the business or investment', used in section 14 (1) of the Income Tax Act, 2058-which has puzzled tax payers and tax officers and has much judicial ink poured over it. This will be analyzed in light of few cases decided by the Supreme Court of Nepal and few leading cases from U.K. and India on onlending arrangements.

title: Development of Financing through Bank Asset Securitization: A Study of Policy and Market Readiness
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Development of Financing through Bank Asset Securitization: A Study of Policy and Market Readiness
detail.abstract: Since its introduction in the 1970s, securitization practices have evolved to facilitate various funding needs for projects with potential cash flows. Derived from traditional lending, securitization is conducted through a re-engineering scheme that separates institutional risk from the risk of the underlying assets. Generally, assets that can be securitized are those with potential future cash flows, such as mortgages, auto loans, credit card receivables, royalties, and others. In Indonesia, securitization practices began to develop in the 2000s. Although institutional infrastructure is not yet fully in place, the increasing funding needs to drive economic growth, amidst the limitations of traditional funding sources (bank credit), have prompted various parties to initiate the use of non-traditional financing sources. One such source is asset securitization. This study seeks to examine and identify several issues faced in the asset securitization process in banks, including regulatory, institutional, infrastructure, and ecosystem aspects. The research is expected to complement existing references on securitization practices in Indonesia. Additionally, some recommendations proposed are expected to drive initiatives to complete and refine various aspects necessary in the securitization process.

title: R-Squareds in the Cross Section and Time Series
affiliations: , Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, Warwick Business School and University of Brescia - Department of Economics and Management

detail.title: R-Squareds in the Cross Section and Time Series
detail.abstract:
We exploit the link between systematic volatility and betas in linear factor models to show that the R-squared of a cross-sectional (CS) second-pass regression of test asset risk premia on factor loadings can be factorized into two components. The first component captures the factor model's average time-series (TS) fit across test assets, while the second component reflects the maximum risk-return trade-off of the model's optimal factor portfolio (OFP) relative to that of the test assets.
Our factorization explains why adding systematic factors to a model may reduce the TS fit: the new OFP hedges away systematic risk and explains less of the test assets' volatility. Our decomposition also explains why weak factors, while not systematic, can improve pricing: they have higher information ratios than the factors in existing models.
For example, the improvement in pricing performance going from the capital asset pricing model to three-, five-, and six-factor Fama-French specifications is mainly due to an increase in the relative risk-return trade-off of the factors of the larger models, and not to an improvement in the average TS fit. Furthermore, we employ our novel decomposition to  show that factors other than the market enter the `factor zoo' mainly because they are profitable in sample, not because they are pervasive. The market, on the other hand, dominates all other factors in terms of its pervasiveness. Finally, our out-of-sample results provide an interpretation for the longevity of the CAPM and for the lack of robustness and associated skepticism regarding all the empirically-motivated pricing factors that have been proposed in literature.

title: Hartwick's Rule Revisited: Sustainability, Substitution, and Collapse
affiliations: and MacEwan University, School of Business

detail.title: Hartwick's Rule Revisited: Sustainability, Substitution, and Collapse
detail.abstract: Hartwick's Rule suggests that reinvesting resource rents in capital can sustain consumption over time. But this relies on the assumption that capital can fully substitute for natural resources, an assumption increasingly challenged by evidence. This paper revises Hartwick's Rule by allowing for limited substitutability between capital and resource inputs. Using a CES production function, we show that under imperfect substitution, the classical rule fails: output collapses even if all resource rents are saved. We propose a revised rule that directs investment toward renewable capital that replaces the lost resource flow. If substitution starts early, the economy avoids collapse and sustains consumption. This is the paper's key contribution: a formal, tractable model showing when and why Hartwick's rule breaks down, and how a transition-oriented investment strategy can restore sustainability. The revised rule strengthens the case for refining genuine savings indicators and aligning resource revenues with long-term capacity building.

title: The Combustion Paradox: Autonomous Hydrological Security and Soil-Moisture Preservation via Multi-Constellation Telemetry and Vision Transformers

detail.title: The Combustion Paradox: Autonomous Hydrological Security and Soil-Moisture Preservation via Multi-Constellation Telemetry and Vision Transformers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. This research was conducted independently as a grassroots technological and sociological intervention under the FTOH (For The Only Home) Research Collaborative.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Field deployments and sociological interventions involving local agricultural practitioners were conducted in strict adherence to ethical guidelines for grassroots research. All community interactions were non-punitive and voluntary. Participating farmers provided explicit informed consent prior to engaging in the "Mutual Cooperation Pacts" and allowing the deployment of IoT sensor nodes on their agricultural plots. No sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) was published, and all data was utilized solely for the facilitation of subsidized agricultural alternatives and environmental monitoring.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific financial grant from any centralized funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was executed as an independent, self-funded frugal innovation initiative by the FTOH Research Collaborative, operating with localized administrative and logistical mandates from the Assistant Director of Agriculture (Egra) and Block Development Officers in Purba Medinipur, West Bengal.

detail.abstract: Agricultural stubble burning across the Indo-Gangetic Plain and its eastward extension into West Bengal constitutes one of the most thermodynamically destructive, institutionally misclassified, and hydro-economically consequential land management failures in contemporary South Asian agriculture. Quantified at an annual macroeconomic hemorrhage of approximately $24 billion USD, the crisis has been persistently, and dangerously, reduced in policy discourse to an air quality emergency-a framing that, while epidemiologically significant in its own right, systematically conceals the permanent, compounding destruction of the regional hydrological architecture. This paper argues that the dominant enforcement-centered policy paradigm-satellite surveillance followed by administrative fines-is structurally incoherent when applied to an 'economic captive': a smallholder farmer for whom the cost of a matchstick (1) is offset by a 600 labor invoice for mechanized residue management. Project SATARK (Sanskrit: satark, meaning 'Alert') proposes and operationalizes a fundamentally different intervention logic. SATARK functions not as a fire-detection alarm but as a precision logistics bridge-a real-time, AI-augmented supply chain that dispatches field machinery to vulnerable agricultural plots before combustion occurs, thereby interrupting the causal chain between harvest economics and soil-hydraulic degradation. The system integrates NASA FIRMS multi-constellation satellite telemetry, geostationary backfill from the GK-2A sensor suite, a Cascaded SwinIR Vision Transformer for predictive harvest-window mapping via NDVI time-series analysis, and a distributed ESP8266/LoRa IoT ground-truth swarm to validate remote sensing signals against in-situ micro-climatic measurements. This synthesis details the thermodynamic physics underlying the hydrological destruction pathway-encompassing black carbon albedo collapse, soil organic matter (SOM) pyrolytic annihilation, post-combustion hydrophobic surface formation, and thermal inversion-driven micro-climate disruption-and maps these physical processes directly onto the resulting groundwater depletion spiral and irrigation inflation trap that perpetuates farmer debt. The paper documents the Phase 1 Kolaghat Pilot in Purba Medinipur, West Bengal, validates the system's capacity to detect sub-50 MW micro-fires invisible to state-operated monitoring infrastructure, and outlines the institutional integration pathway secured through the Block Development Officer and Assistant Director of Agriculture. The central thesis is axiomatic: code without sociology is noise. SATARK is the synthesis of both.

title: The Wrong Reference Price: Trading Strategy and the Disposition Effect
affiliations: The University of San Diego - Knauss School of Business

detail.title: The Wrong Reference Price: Trading Strategy and the Disposition Effect
detail.abstract: Measuring the disposition effect requires a reference price to classify positions as gains or losses. For multi-purchase positions, candidate references can disagree, yet the standard convention uses the volume-weighted average price (VWAP). Using population-level data, we show that the relevant reference depends on how the position was built. Investors who bought down into losing positions anchor on their last purchase price; investors who bought up into winning positions anchor on the VWAP. The same individual, holding both types on the same day, switches references; sell rates spike at each strategy's predicted breakeven. These breakeven-triggered sales cost 197 basis points in forgone returns. Because the disposition effect causes investors to hold losers, subsequent purchases disproportionately occur below the VWAP, making buy-down positions the majority. The VWAP reference, therefore, understates the disposition effect for most multi-purchase positions: under a strategy-conditional reference price, experienced investors exhibit a disposition effect more than four times larger than previously documented.

title: The Zero-profit Substitution in Contests with Heterogeneous Costs: Applications to Oil Extraction and Blockchain Security
affiliations: University of Exeter

detail.title: The Zero-profit Substitution in Contests with Heterogeneous Costs: Applications to Oil Extraction and Blockchain Security
detail.abstract: In any Tullock contest with heterogeneous costs, the standard zero-profit substitution compresses three distinct objects-total expenditure, incremental acquisition cost, and deployment level-into one scalar. This article derives the conditions under which the compression fails, bounds the error, and characterises the welfare loss. The leading application is proof-of-work blockchain security, where Budish (2025) substitutes a zero-profit condition to derive a blockreward constraint. Under heterogeneous mining costs, the substitution understates acquisition cost, and the article derives a corrected security condition that depends on cost-schedule shape. The model nests Budish as a special case.

title: The Collapse of Scarcity Economics
affiliations: University of St. Thomas - School of Law (Minnesota)

detail.title: The Collapse of Scarcity Economics
detail.abstract: Traditional economic frameworks assume scarcity-constrained equilibrium, wherein capital, labor, and resources interact within finite boundaries. Artificial intelligence and robotics introduce production functions that decouple growth from labor constraints, thus fundamentally challenging this foundational assumption. Building on the author's prior work, this Article argues that the convergence of AI-driven automation, zero-marginal-cost production, and exponential scaling renders obsolete not merely individual occupations but the institutional architectures that depend upon scarcity as an organizing principle. The Article systematically demonstrates how the core propositions of neoclassical, behavioral, information-theoretic, general-equilibrium, and New Institutional economics expire in the face of computational abundance. It develops a theoretical framework for understanding abundance as a structural economic condition and proposes that the emerging economy requires governance mechanisms designed for what the author has elsewhere termed Computative Economics-economic science explicitly designed for a world in which intelligence is abundant, perfect, and self-improving.

title: The Modeling Route to Structural Generalization
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: The Modeling Route to Structural Generalization
detail.abstract: Statistical approximation-empirical risk minimisation over large hypothesis classes trained on massive corpora-is the dominant and most empirically successful route to high-capacity machine intelligence. We accept this premise. The question we address is not whether statistical approximation is productive, but whether it is sufficient: what additional structural properties, if any, must learned operators exhibit to qualify as genuinely general? We formalise learned models as measure-valued operators and propose four operator-level criteria for structural generalization: (i) symmetry equivariance, (ii) systematic compositionality, (iii) counterfactual robustness, and (iv) distributional-shift stability. We then prove three impossibility theorems that sharpen the debate by characterising what observational empirical risk minimisation (ERM) can and cannot certify: Theorem 5.2 (Causal Impossibility) shows that no algorithm trained only on observational data can guarantee uniform counterfactual robustness over non-trivial intervention classes; Theorem 7.2 (IB-Equivariance Underdetermination) shows that information-bottleneck optimal representations need not be equivariant, so compression objectives underdetermine structural abstraction; and Theorem 9.4 (Main Impossibility) shows that no observational ERM procedure can simultaneously guarantee equivariance and counterfactual robustness across all observationally compatible data-generating processes (via a universal minimax causal lower bound, Theorem 9.1, and an adversarial equivariance-gap construction, Theorem 9.2). Scope note. All impossibility results are worst-case over observational equivalence classes and adversarial distributions. They establish what cannot be certified from observational ERM alone-not that structural failure will occur on every distribution. The distinction between "cannot certify" and "will fail" is maintained throughout. Theorem 5.2 (and Theorem 9.1) are universal over all algorithms and sample sizes. Theorem 9.2 is existential: it guarantees a high-defect ERM minimizer exists, not that every minimizer has large defect. The joint Main Impossibility (Theorem 9.4) combines these two distinct quantifier structures; see Remark 9.3 for the precise statement.

title: Filling the Tank: How China Aims to Wean Itself Off Foreign Oil

detail.title: Filling the Tank: How China Aims to Wean Itself Off Foreign Oil
detail.abstract: China's energy self-sufficiency has come under a microscope in the wake of the Iran Crisis and the semi-closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Since nearly half of China's oil imports are derived from the Persian Gulf, a serious disruption to China's economy may seem likely if the crisis is not resolved. But the truth is that China has been stepping up its production of domestic oil and natural gas in preparation for this precise moment. Around one quarter of oil demand in China is currently met by domestic supply. In fact, domestic crude oil production reached a record-high of 215 million metric tons in 2025, and 105 million tons of new crude oil capacity were added from 2021 to 2025. China is also the fourth-largest natural gas producer in the world, with 260 billion cubic meters of natural gas produced in 2025. Overall, total oil and gas output in China surpassed 400 million metric tons of oil in 2024, while total power generation exceeded 10 trillion kilowatt-hours, which was a 5.7% increase from 2023. Thus, China's policy is to "fill the tank" as much as possible with domestic oil and gas, which will help the country weather the storm from the latest Middle East fracas. This article overviews the major advances made by Chinese domestic oil and gas producers while highlighting efforts to reduce emissions from fuel production.

title: On the Mathematics of Structural Generalization: Symmetry, Combinatorial Impossibility, and the Architectural Gap in Transformers
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: On the Mathematics of Structural Generalization: Symmetry, Combinatorial Impossibility, and the Architectural Gap in Transformers
detail.abstract: We examine claims about structural generalization through three mathematical lenses-symmetry, combinatorics, and optimisation-organised around three questions of strictly increasing difficulty, with an explicit separation between existence (representation) and learnability (optimisation). On combinatorial feasibility, we establish a sharp lower bound showing that any corpus covering every permutation orbit in sequence space must contain an astronomically large number of sequences-physically unachievable at realistic vocabulary sizes. This symmetry exchangeability gap forces any successful learner to exploit structural priors rather than exhaustive tabulation. On representational capacity, we demonstrate that a single attention head with lowrank weight matrices suffices to separate compositionally distinct sequences under mild positional encoding conditions, establishing that the relevant compositional functions lie within the transformer hypothesis class. On learnability, we prove that in the neural tangent kernel (NTK) / lazy regime, gradient descent is biased toward lower-complexity co-occurrence solutions over compositionally structured ones under both squared and cross-entropy loss. Conflating representational capacity with learnability is identified as the primary source of imprecision in debates about transformer generalization. We formalise an architectural gap via four compositional generalisation axioms. Standard transformers violate the first axiom structurally; a proposed role-factorised variant satisfies it by construction. All theoretical predictions are stated as falsifiable conjectures with a concrete empirical validation protocol.

title: From Xs to Boxes: Toward a More Radical Graphical Metaphor for Progressives
affiliations: University of Kentucky College of Law

detail.title: From Xs to Boxes: Toward a More Radical Graphical Metaphor for Progressives
detail.abstract: The Edgeworth Box provides progressives with a graphical language that can be used to make a powerful case for radical and efficient redistribution of wealth via taxation and law reform. The box also makes it easy to show that price regulation and antitrust are of much more limited use in redistributing wealth. Progressives should embrace the graphical language of the box and give up partial equilibrium scissors graphs, which provide an incomplete picture of policy options for redistribution of wealth.

title: Quantum Dynamics of OECD Financial Markets (2000–2025): Schrödinger-Type Modeling and Volatility Forecasts to 2050
affiliations: University of Ain Temouchent

detail.title: Quantum Dynamics of OECD Financial Markets (2000–2025): Schrödinger-Type Modeling and Volatility Forecasts to 2050
detail.abstract: This study develops a quantum Schrödinger-type framework for modeling financial volatility and tail risk in major OECD equity markets from 2000 to 2025, with long-horizon projections extending to 2050. By integrating quantum diffusion, wave function amplitude, and probability interference effects, the framework captures stylized facts such as volatility clustering, fat tails, and abrupt regime shifts that classical stochastic models often fail to replicate. Empirical results indicate that quantum parameters, including the effective Planck constant and quantum diffusion coefficient, exhibit significant amplification during crisis periods, driving extreme market outcomes and persistent structural volatility. Comparative analyses with classical models (GARCH, Heston) show that the quantum approach consistently improves Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) accuracy, enhances tail coverage, and reduces exceedances, offering robust risk measurement tools for regulators and portfolio managers. Scenario-based projections reveal nonlinear amplification of volatility under systemic shocks, highlighting the framework's applicability for long-term forecasting, stress testing, and policy assessment. Robustness checks, including time-varying potentials, stochastic quantum mass, and regime-switching dynamics, confirm the model's stability and interpretability. Overall, the quantum approach provides a conceptually rich and practically actionable methodology for understanding complex financial market dynamics in both normal and extreme conditions.

title: The preferences of the citizens in Athens Metropolitan Area towards economic investment in nearby forests: A Discrete Choice Experiment with Time Discounting
affiliations: University of Reading and University of Reading - School of Agriculture, Policy & Development - Department of Agricultural and Food Economics

detail.title: The preferences of the citizens in Athens Metropolitan Area towards economic investment in nearby forests: A Discrete Choice Experiment with Time Discounting
detail.abstract: This study deploys a choice experiment survey to investigate the preferences of citizens in the Athens Metropolitan Area (AMA) regarding the planned financial investment in forest regime initiatives, including reforestation, fire protection, and recreational infrastructure. It estimates the economic value that citizens put on environmental forest non-market goods and services, during a period when they feel both socioeconomic and environmental pressures. Alternativetreatments of time and time discounting are considered within our models. We find that respondents seem to heavily discount both payments and benefits but the payment discounting being at a much higher rate. Our preferred model is one of asymmetric exponential discounting. Our findings align with existing literature on the importance of ecosystem services and infrastructure in urban contexts.

title: A Machine Learning Approach to Estimate Food Insecurity (FIES) and Social Exclusion (SESI) from Socioeconomic Indicators
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Granada

detail.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Estimate Food Insecurity (FIES) and Social Exclusion (SESI) from Socioeconomic Indicators
detail.abstract: This study leverages data from national statistical institute APIs and other public sources to develop predictive models for three key proxies of social vul- nerability: the prevalence of moderate and severe food insecurity (FIES) and the Social Exclusion Synthetic Indicator (SESI). Using supervised machine learning algorithms, Gradient Boosting Regressor, XGBoost, and CatBoost, we estimate FIES prevalence with low root mean squared error (RMSE) and classify SESI with up to 75% accuracy. Key predictors include per capita rent, average age, education level, unemployment rates, and social isolation indicators. Results are visualized through a municipal-level dashboard for the Madrid Autonomous Community, providing monthly map-based predictions. The findings support data-driven policy design to address food insecurity and social exclusion

title: Sanitation, wastewater and solid waste disposal practices in five communities in Kumasi, Ghana
affiliations: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana - Regional Water and Environmental Sanitation Centre, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sanitation, wastewater and solid waste disposal practices in five communities in Kumasi, Ghana
detail.abstract: Inadequate sanitation is a major global health risk, particularly in developing countries. This study investigated household sanitation practices, wastewater and solid waste disposal practices in five communities within Kumasi, Ghana. A cross-sectional survey conducted using structured questionnaires administered to 369 purposively and randomly selected households. Demographic and socioeconomic factors such as education, occupation, religion, household size, and type of home influenced sanitation choices. The results revealed significant sanitation challenges, including widespread use of public or shared latrines, often located near drinking water sources. Approximately 59% of the household lacked drainage systems, and 67% disposed of wastewater directly into open spaces such as gutters, streets, or backyards. In terms of solid waste disposal practices, 72% of households owned garbage containers, others resorted to burning, burying, or dumping waste into gutters. Notably, 35% of respondents had drinking water sources located within 30 meters of waste disposal sites. These findings highlight the urgent need for improved sanitation infrastructure and public education on safe waste disposal and its health implications. To address this public health threat, the government should mandate landlords in city slums to provide latrines for tenants, enhance waste management systems and promote behaviour change through community engagement. Further research is needed to assess the long-term effects of on-site sanitation systems on groundwater quality.

title: Data-Efficient Learning Through Prior World Models: A Formal Framework for Structural Generalization
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: Data-Efficient Learning Through Prior World Models: A Formal Framework for Structural Generalization
detail.abstract: Humans acquire robust predictive models from remarkably little experience, while modern machine-learning systems require orders of magnitude more data. This gap originates in rich prior knowledge biological agents deploy as structured world models-internal predictive simulators of environment dynamics. We develop a framework for Prior World Model Learning (PWML), in which a reusable dynamics prior is acquired through self-supervised pretraining and adapted to new environments with minimal data. We make four contributions. First, a formal framework: precise terminology, a hierarchical Bayesian meta-prior formulation, and a modular Meta-Prior World Model (MPWM) combining JEPA-style pretraining with bilevel meta-learning. Second, we synthesise the cognitive science of human data efficiency-core knowledge, compositionality, causal reasoning, episodic memory-mapping each to its machine-learning counterpart. Third, JEPA-style predictive-in-representation objectives provide a signal for dynamics-prior learning conditionally: when the target is stable, the predictor capacity-limited, and collapse-avoidance holds; shortcuts persist when violated. Fourth, we validate MPWM on five families spanning linear and nonlinear regimes: bimodal SSMs (Reptile +10.2% over pretrain-only), Van der Pol oscillators (8× RMSE reduction), compositional multi-body dynamics (85-88% reduction), causal adaptation (+67% at 5-shot), and a nonlinear MLP pendulum family where the Reptile advantage over pretrain-only grows to +23.4%, confirming that meta-learning benefits are amplified in the nonlinear regime. A loss-menu ablation further shows that combining dynamics and JEPA-style representation losses yields an additional 8.1% OOD improvement over dynamics loss alone. Four formal results position MPWM against the Structural Generalization Axioms. Theorem 1 gives a KL-regularized stability bound for action-conditioned adaptation. Corollary 1 strengthens this to a truth-relative identifiability guarantee under realizability and feasibility: the adapted model converges to the true action-conditioned law as interventional data grows. Theorem 2 proves that the observational impossibility vanishes exponentially in interventional sample size under a fixed uniformly separating intervention, a finite candidate class, and a bounded log-likelihood-ratio condition. Proposition 1 gives a conditional grammar-based sample-complexity bound O(gd 0 log(gd 0)), reducing to O(g log g) when perprimitive complexity is bounded. This paper develops a constructive response to recent impossibility results: where unconstrained observational ERM cannot provide the required guarantees, we propose structured priors, interventional data, and meta-learning as escape mechanisms.

title: Universal Basic Income: Consumption, Human Capital, and Labor Supply
affiliations: Radboud University Nijmegen - Institute for Management Research, Radboud University Nijmegen - Institute for Management Research, Radboud University Nijmegen - Institute for Management Research, Radboud University Nijmegen - Institute for Management Research, Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences and Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Universal Basic Income: Consumption, Human Capital, and Labor Supply
detail.abstract: Universal basic income (UBI) has not been implemented as a permanent, economy-wide policy, making its long-run effects difficult to evaluate empirically. Existing evidence relies primarily on structural models and short-run field experiments. We study the long-run behavioral effects of UBI by combining a calibrated life-cycle model with laboratory evidence on consumption, human capital accumulation, and labor supply. We show that behavioral responses deviate from the optimal control benchmark through over-investment in human capital and reduced labor supply and reduce lifetime utility, implying that UBI-induced behavioral adjustments may be inefficient. UBI increases lifetime utility purely through the transfer but does not raise welfare through optimizing behavioral adjustment.

title: Beyond Market Incentives: Linking Ecology and Democracy in Corporate Governance—Political Challenges of Tax Policies in France and Europe
affiliations: University of Toulouse

detail.title: Beyond Market Incentives: Linking Ecology and Democracy in Corporate Governance—Political Challenges of Tax Policies in France and Europe
detail.abstract: While current corporate governance frameworks of corporate limit the integration of environmental considerations into corporate-level decision-making, this paper argues that public policy must promote corporate democratization as a prerequisite for effective ecological governance. Adopting an institutionalist perspective and drawing on a qualitative typology combined with a lexicometric analysis of various existing tax disincentives and incentives (tax advantages and subsidies) aimed at protecting the environment and/or targeting businesses, this article examines the challenges for public incentive policies (public aids and tax disincentives) in articulating ecology and democracy in corporate governance. To ensure that corporate ecological governance is not viewed solely through the prism of market efficiency, this article highlights the need to link it to questions of workplace democracy, with a view to transforming public policies so that they are explicitly designed to influence corporate governance.
